column1: # TITLE: The anticancer effects of tanshinone I in human non-small-cell lung cancer
# SUMMARY: Tanshinones are the major bioactive compounds of Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (Danshen)
column3: which are used in many therapeutic remedies in Chinese traditional medicine. We investigated the anticancer effects of tanshinones on the highly invasive human lung adenocarcinoma cell line
column4: CL1-5. Tanshinone I significantly inhibited migration
column6: and gelatinase activity in macrophage-conditioned medium (CM)-stimulated CL1-5 cells in vitro and also reduced the tumorigenesis and metastasis in CL1-5-bearing severe combined immunodeficiency mice. Unlike tanshinone IIA
column8: tanshinone I had no significant cytotoxicity. Real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RTQ-PCR)
column10: and an electrophoretic mobility shift assay revealed that tanshinone I reduces the transcriptional activity of interleukin-8 (IL-8)
column11: the angiogenic factor involved in cancer metastasis
column12: by attenuating the DNA-binding activity of activator protein-1 and nuclear factor kappaB in CM-stimulated CL1-5 cells. Microarray and pathway analysis of tumor-related genes identified the differentially expressed genes responding to tanshinone I
column13: and these results were validated by RTQ-PCR. The responsive genes included human platelet-derived growth factor beta chain
column21: and collagen type IV; these genes may be associated with the Ras MAPK and Rac1 signaling pathways. These results suggest that tanshinone I exhibits anticancer effects both in vitro and in vivo
column22: and that these effects are mediated at least partly through the IL-8
column24: and Rac1 signaling pathways. Keywords: treatment with dose respone
